title: Compiler-owned GF(2) polynomial packed core
objective: Implement canonical compiler-owned bit-packed GF(2)[x] storage and source-transparent read-only traversal, XOR, shifts, equality, formatting, and serialization primitives without changing the public polynomial API or shared FFI

handoff.summary: Adds an immutable canonical BitPolynomialStorage with 64 low-to-high GF(2) coefficients per uint64 word, versioned minimal serialization, Sage-style formatting, and source-transparent borrowed-record kernels for validation, coefficient access, population count, equality, XOR, and left/right shifts. CPython, Sage.js dynamic fallback, and AOT native execution agree at 0/63/64/65 boundaries and malformed writes remain transactional. The retained degree-262143 benchmark records 32768 packed bytes versus 2097152 bytes for one uint64 per coefficient, native XOR near 20 ms, native word shifts near 18 ms, and native weight near 1 ms on linux-x64.
risks: The source-transparent compiler currently lacks uint64 bitwise operators, so XOR deliberately performs 64 arithmetic bit steps per word; a future representation-level compiler primitive can optimize this without changing the storage contract.
Only linux-x64 execution was available in this lane; required linux-arm64, Windows x64, and macOS arm64 validation remains CI or integration work.
This is a disjoint core lane and does not modify the public polynomial API, production native-kernel manifest, dispatch profiles, or external NTL integration.
next_steps: Integration must add src/lib/sagejs/kernels/polynomial/gf2_packed.py to the polynomial-native-kernels owner in architecture/package-graph.json before architecture:check.
Adopt BitPolynomialStorage as the public GF(2)[x] canonical representation in a separate integration lane, with retained Sage differential tests.
Add a generated opaque NTL GF2X resource for measured large multiplication, division, GCD, and factorization crossovers while preserving packed core storage at the public boundary.
Consider a general compiler uint64 bitwise intrinsic/lowering only after this storage contract lands; this lane intentionally changes no compiler internals.
